speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your rash and recent symptoms, can you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail, such as whether it is flat, raised, or blister-like? Additionally, have you noticed any specific triggers or new medications that might have preceded these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression from a facial rash sparing the mouth to a body rash after a prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea is highly characteristic of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). Do you recall if the facial rash had a distinct "slapped cheek" appearance before the trunk rash appeared, and have you been exposed to anyone with similar symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities after a viral prodrome, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
